newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end slightly higher, mirroring Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end slightly higher, mirroring Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly higiher on Thursday after drifting in parallel with activity on Wall Street.
"I think the market is very much on hold while waiting for (fourth quarter) earnings reports. Volume was sparse, and the bourse ended up because of a late turnaround in the Dow," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 1.67 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,654.66. Total volume, was 109.3 million shares, of which cross trades accounted for about a third.
Traders noted that share prices zigzagged through the session, generally mirroring the Dow Industrials.

"I don't think the market is worried by possible fallout from U.S. non-farm payroll figures tomorrow, not now the Federal Open Market Committee decided not to raise U.S. interest rates," the trader added, referring to the Federal Reserve panel's decision on Wednesday.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 26.16 points, or 0.39 percent, at 6,773.06 points.

The IPC had opened lower in a delayed reaction to falls in Mexican American Depository Receipts on Wednesday, when local markets were closed for a holiday. Share prices later recovered, slumped and rebounded once more towards the close.
"There's a bit of a time lag, but we basically followed the Dow today," a trader said.
Market heavyweight Telmex L shares closed down four centavos (1 cent) at 14.62 pesos ($1.87) in Mexico, while its ADRs ended up 1/2 at 37-1/4.
"Local shares and ADRs were out of synch after we were closed yesterday, then the peso waivered during the day and gave rise to arbitrage trading between the two," a trader said.
On the broad market, 102 shares changed hands, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 54 to 31.
Telecommunications company Iusacel topped the gainers, up 1.80 pesos (23 cents) to 8.70 pesos ($1.11).
A Iusacel source told Reuters that institutional investors appeared to be buying the stock on speculation that official approval was forthcoming for a management takeover by Bell Atlantic.
Traders noted that Iusacel had been inactive since Jan. 28 and had lagged behind advances by its ADR, which closed flat at 9-1/4.
Most heavily traded gainer was financial group Banacci A shares, up 26 centavos (3 cents) to 14.76 ($1.87) after a hefty cross trade by the group's own brokerage.
Dealers said the decliners list was topped by second- and third-tier stocks after relatively small trades that did not necessarily reveal market trends.

Most heavily traded decliner was retail chain Comerci, off 12 centavos (2 cents) at 7.02 pesos (90 cents). Traders said the retail sector suffered after recent figures showing sales at self-service and department stores in December slumped in year-on-year terms.
